Cost of an op = its busy time plus the GPU idle gap before it, so op costs sum to the step time. Each kernel's SOL is one of two unrelated claims, labeled in its tooltip. Analytic estimate: a floor computed from declared shapes, precision ceilings and traffic assumptions, it can be wrong if an assumption does not hold. NCU measured: this kernel's own achieved utilization from an NCU profile, used when no analytic estimate applies (exact and transferred matches labeled). A kernel can show both: a low analytic estimate does not mean the kernel is inefficient if NCU separately measures it near peak utilization, that NCU number describes the real work, the analytic one may have undercounted it. Operations missing both sources are gray. Incomplete table groups show n/a. D2D copies count a payload read and write, host transfers require a link profile. The forward reference excludes intermediate materialization and checkpoint writes. Draft query work is excluded when its shape is unknown. These optimistic roofline references omit finite-workload latency and cache effects. Timeline x SOL = kernel duration / SOL. Table x SOL = attributed cost / SOL, with overlapping busy time counted once. Idle kinds: host (launch call returned after the GPU went idle), in_graph (between nodes of one graph), launch_latency (op was queued and still waited). Graph kernels without a CUPTI launch record are assigned to the latest graph launch that has no kernels of its own, so they get its phase.
